We didn't receive salary for three or four months, but I never -- it never crossed my mind to leave the Army of Republika Srpska, and the same situation happened during the sanctions when we also didn't receive any salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 47, witness said, line 18, the witness said, "I never thought about my salary."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A while ago, Mr. Saxon showed you -- actually, I suppose quoted from your personal file your request for the payment for unused annual leave in the period 1992, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document 1D11-0614 on our screens. That's one portion of the personnel file of Mr. Malcic. We don't have an English translation. I'm going to read a portion and then ask the witness to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document that we see on the screen has the following heading: "General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel issues, confidential number 03/2-17-178, 16th of October, 1998." I'm going to read only one portion which says that: "Pursuant to the request of Malcic Stojan, Colonel, I hereby issue this certificate whereby this sector confirms that Stojan Malcic, father's name Petar, born on the 1st of February, 1946 -- 1948, discharged the duties of the chief of personnel administration in the sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel issues in the Main Staff of the Army Republika Srpska until retirement. "Due to being engaged in the carrying out of tasks in the combat area, the above-named was unable to use his annual leaves for the years of 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995." This was signed by the chief of the personnel administration, Lieutenant-Colonel Dane Maric. Mr. Malcic, from this document can you tell us to which army you belonged before the retirement?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who issued this document?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the personnel administration, Colonel Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I turn to this document to be admitted into evidence as MFI'd document, and I would just like to add that I have no further questions for Mr. Malcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be marked for identification and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be D00315, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Malcic, I have a question for you. I listened carefully to what you have said over these last few days, in particular with relation to your status in the VRS, and I do, after all this, have a question. You might be able to answer it. In your view, why were you being paid by the Yugoslav Army? What was the reason for it?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1992 when I was exchanged and when I left the prison, I heard that a decision had been taken by the highest political leaderships -- leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia for all the JNA units to withdraw to the territory of the FRY. The active servicemen and civilians serving in the JNA who remained part of the army in Bosnia-Herzegovina, because at the time nobody knew how this army was going to be called, it was said that they would receive their salaries and other fringe benefits as if they had continued to serve in the JNA; and the rules applicable for that, for the payment of salary, would be the ones valid at that period. I think this was announced in the media. I think on the 5th of May, 1992. And that was before the Army of Republika Srpska was formed. Why this decision was taken, I don't know. I can only surmise that the FRY was proclaimed the successor of the SFRY and that the Yugoslav Army was to become the successor of the JNA. Therefore, I suppose that that was the reason for their taking this decision. Believe me, as a professional it would have been easier for me if they had suspended all the payments to active-duty officers at the time, because we already had our government. We had our budget. And we had enough funds to pay all the servicemen and the new servicemen that were joining the Army of Republika Srpska. As it was, we just had to do dual work. We remained there because we wanted to be with our own people, with our brothers, with our friends, with our relatives with whom I grew up, and we all wanted to defend our birthplaces, and we didn't want to put ourselves in a position to be expelled from that area by anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did understand this. You wanted to stay in Republika Srpska, and you wanted to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska, but I'm only half convinced by your explanation inasmuch as you say that a decision was taken at the highest level and that the decision in question said that the servicemen staying in the former territories of Yugoslavia would keep being paid by the Yugoslav Army, but that is not quite true, accurate, is it? This is only true for the, let's say, Serbian servicemen. I mean, the servicemen who were Croats who decided to fight in the Croatian army, they were no longer paid by the Yugoslav Army. Neither were the Croatian servicemen who later on served in the Croatian army in Bosnia. So which is the reason why Serbian servicemen like you kept being paid whilst they were no longer in the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I answered your question, I think, on my first day of testimony. All of us who remained serving in the JNA pending the order for those units to withdraw to the FRY were being paid by the FRY during that period. As for the Croat officers who joined the Army of Republic of Croatia or the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as Muslim officers who joined Territorial Defence units as they were called at the beginning and which was later re-named the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in early 1991 and 1992, they left their establishment positions in the JNA of their own volition, and under the law they were given five days for a document on termination of their service in the JNA to be issued. However, there were both Muslim and Croat officers who stayed until the end with the JNA, who later joined the Army of Republika Srpska and who eventually, some of them, withdrew to the territory of the FRY and continued to receive payments from the federal budget of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hadn't understood that as well, but this is still no explanation for the fact that the VRS servicemen and officers kept being paid by the Yugoslav Army. Unless you tell me that you were still in the Yugoslav Army, which is what you appear to say, but I don't think you want to say. So this is not a very compelling explanation. Maybe you have no other explanation.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem was with the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Your Honour. I think that the witness gave a very precise answer on page 50, lines 5 to 8. He said that he didn't know why this decision was taken. He can only suppose that the FRY declared itself a successor of the SFRY, and I truly believe, Honourable Judge Picard, that he did answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then I fail to understand. Well, I still don't understand why the Yugoslav Army kept paying officers belonging to another army, an army of another country. The fact that there were states that succeeded the former Yugoslavia, say the Republic of Serbia, is not an explanation that I would deem the proper one. But it may be that you don't know, Witness.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this -- well, I wanted to say later, after I retired, all members of the Yugoslav People's Army, who before the outbreak of war were there, applied to the personnel administration of the VJ to receive certificates that would help them to get pensions in their respective newly formed states. I know that because I personally collected such documents and sent to my friends in Sarajevo. That means that the personnel administration, they had DP 2 forms, and they kept it on their archives. I don't know who proclaimed this administration to be the successor, but we all appealed and addressed this administration from the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia in order to regulate our pension problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down, and travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Do we then postpone to tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, our plan was to work with this witness tomorrow as well, and for that reason we did not call any witnesses to appear tomorrow. That is to say that in view of the notification that we have received, we will not have any witnesses before 12th of April. I think that's a Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Notification you received from ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm talking about the next week. We received information that there will be no sitting of this Trial Chamber. As for tomorrow, we knew that a normal day was scheduled. At the beginning when we had Pre-Trial Conference, I think that we said that we shall -- that there will be no sitting on the 26th and 29th -- excuse me. I think 26th, 29th, and 30th. The remaining days are 31st and the 1st. That is before Easter holidays. And according to that, we created our schedule according to which we're going to bring our first witness on the 12th of April, that is, after Easter holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What about the 31st and the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we received information -- well, Your Honour, truly, I think we received information there will be no sitting prior to the 12th of April. If it is my mistake, I assume full responsibility. But I think that that is what was conveyed to us, that these two days, 31st and 1st, there will be no sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Lukic, I won't take the matter much further. Then the matter stands adjourned to the 12th of April. And I don't -- do I have -- I don't seem to have the April calendar. I'm not quite sure whether we're sitting in the morning or -- I think it is in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At 9.00 in the morning. As I don't have the calendar, I also don't know in which courtroom. Does anybody know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In courtroom II, 9.00 in the morning. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of April, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
